[[File:Alex Ferguson.jpg|thumb|upright|right|alt=Alex Ferguson as manager of Manchester United in 2006jejsiisjs|[[Alex Ferguson]] won a record 13 league championships from 1993 to 2013 as manager of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].]]
The top level of the [[English football league system]] from its formation in 1888 was the [[English Football League|Football League]], until the introduction of a Second Division in 1892 when it became known as the  [[Football League First Division]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.efl.com/-more/all-about-the-efl/history/ |title=The EFL: Who we are |publisher=EFL |access-date=27 April 2023 |archive-date=17 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217193743/https://www.efl.com/-more/all-about-the-efl/history/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This remained the top level of English football until 1992 when it was replaced by the [[Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/history/origins |title=Origins |publisher=Premier League |access-date=19 March 2023 |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319005641/https://www.premierleague.com/history/origins |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nationalfootballmuseum.com/collectionsnews/pl-1992/ |title=Objects of the week: The formation of the Premier League |publisher=National Football Museum |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=27 April 2023 |first=Uma |last=Ghelani |archive-date=7 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230207104332/https://www.nationalfootballmuseum.com/collectionsnews/pl-1992/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The role of the [[Manager (association football)|manager]] is to select the squad during the league season, develop the tactics of the team and manage potential issues within the squad. Due to the prestige of winning the league championship, the pressures on managers to succeed can be great.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ft.com/content/10689ffc-07cf-11e0-8138-00144feabdc0 |title=What makes a great football manager? |work=Financial Times |date=17 December 2010 |access-date=18 March 2023 |url-access=subscription |first=Neil |last=O'Sullivan |archive-date=18 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318205044/https://www.ft.com/content/10689ffc-07cf-11e0-8138-00144feabdc0 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[William Sudell]] managed [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] to the inaugural championship in [[1888–89 Football League|1888–89]], which they retained the following season, with Suddell becoming the first manager to win multiple championships.{{sfn|Butler|1988|p=12}} Since then, a further 24 managers have won the championship on more than one occasion. [[Alex Ferguson]] won 13 league championships as manager of [[Manchester United]], which is the most a manager has won.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/guardiola-becomes-englands-most-successful-foreign-manager-2022-05-22/ |title=Guardiola becomes England's most successful foreign manager |publisher=Reuters |date=22 May 2022 |access-date=19 March 2023 |first=Simon |last=Evans |archive-date=20 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220720130722/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/guardiola-becomes-englands-most-successful-foreign-manager-2022-05-22/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[George Ramsay (footballer, born 1855)|George Ramsay]] and [[Bob Paisley]] won six league championships as managers of [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] respectively. Nine managers — [[Ted Drake]], [[Bill Nicholson (footballer)|Bill Nicholson]], [[Alf Ramsey]], [[Joe Mercer]], [[Dave Mackay]], [[Bob Paisley]], [[Howard Kendall]], [[Kenny Dalglish]] and [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]] – have won the championship as a player and a manager.<ref name=playermanager>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/20/theknowledge.sport |title=Top-flight champions as both player and manager |work=The Guardian |date=20 April 2005 |access-date=12 March 2023 |first1=James |last1=Dart |first2=Rob |last2=Smyth |archive-date=26 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221226090837/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/20/theknowledge.sport |url-status=live }}</ref> Dalglish is the only one to have won the championship as a [[Player-coach|player-manager]], a feat he achieved in the [[1985–86 Football League|1985–86]], [[1987–88 Football League|1987–88]] and [[1989–90 Football League|1989–90]] seasons.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/7827167.stm |title=When Dalglish did the Double |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 January 2009 |access-date=19 March 2023 |first1=Chris |last1=Bevan |first2=Russell |last2=Barder |archive-date=26 January 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090126030818/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/7827167.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

English managers have won the most championships, with a total of 58 championships won by 38 different managers. Scottish managers are next with 37 championships won by 10 different managers and Spanish managers are third with seven titles, six won by [[Pep Guardiola]] and one by [[Mikel Arteta]]. The last English manager to win the championship was [[Howard Wilkinson]], who led [[Leeds United F.C|Leeds United]] to victory in the [[1991–92 Football League|1991–92 season]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jul/17/leedsunited |title=On Second Thoughts: Leeds United's 1991–92 title |work=The Guardian |date=17 July 2008 |access-date=19 March 2023 |first=Rob |last=Smyth |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319153454/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jul/17/leedsunited |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Arsène Wenger]] became the first manager from outside the British Isles to win the championship when he guided [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] to the [[1997–98 Premier League]] title.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/club/arsenal/359/blog/post/2959355/five-ways-arsenals-arsene-wenger-changed-english-football-forever |title=Five ways Arsenal's Arsene Wenger changed English football forever |publisher=ESPN |date=13 May 2018 |access-date=19 March 2023 |first=Mattias |last=Karen |archive-date=19 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319153105/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/club/arsenal/359/blog/post/2959355/five-ways-arsenals-arsene-wenger-changed-english-football-forever |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Manuel Pellegrini]] became the first manager from outside of Europe to win the championship when he guided [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] to the [[2013–14 Premier League]] title.<ref>{{cite news |date=12 May 2014 |title=City show the right way to win, says Pellegrini |publisher=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-pellegrini-idUKKBN0DS0B620140512 |access-date=28 March 2023 |first=Nick |last=Mulvenney |archive-date=28 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328192549/https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-pellegrini-idUKKBN0DS0B620140512 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Won the League as a player and a manager===

Nine managers have won the championship having previously won the title as a player. Of those, only one, Kenny Dalglish with Liverpool, has won the title in both roles in the same season, triumphing as player-manager in [[1985–86 Football League|1985–86]].
